newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bankers Trust N.Y. economist sees 6.0 pct Fed rate.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust N.Y. economist sees 6.0 pct Fed rate.

text.p: Bankers Trust's New York-based chief global economist John Williams said on Tuesday he expected continued strength in the U.S. economy to lead to further tightenings by the Federal Reserve later this year.
"I think it's going to be at least 6.0 percent by the middle of the year with at least two more Fed tightenings this year," Williams said in a presentation to New Zealand economists and bankers.
The Federal Reserve's last move to raise the rate to 5.50 percent from 5.25 had made no progress in slowing the economy, Williams said.
GDP growth was likely to average 3.0-3.25 percent for the the year, well in excess of the non-inflationary "speed limit" of around 2.0 percent, he said.
"High inflation therefore might be just higher later this summer," Williams said. He added the U.S. dollar, which had weakened over the last two days, may "find its legs" again.
Favourable economic fundamentals had been supporting the cash markets in the U.S. for some time now and a correction in U.S. equities this year was likely, "but nothing cataclysmic".
